description:
Somos un equipo de jóvenes paraguayos, la innovación y la ciencia, unidos por el objetivo de desarrollar soluciones que generen un impacto positivo en nuestra comunidad. una plataforma de inteligencia ambiental enfocada en la integración y armonización de datos satelitales MODIS y VIIRS para el análisis de incendios forestales en Paraguay.

Combinamos creatividad, investigación y desarrollo tecnológico para transformar un desafío real en una propuesta innovadora.
summary:
FIREGUARD is a web platform that shows fire activity in Paraguay on a daily calendar, using real detections from NASA FIRMS.
It addresses the challenge of harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS: the two sensors measure differently (1 km and 375 m pixels, different confidence scales, times in UTC), so they can’t be compared directly. FIREGUARD merges both into a single daily record, converts times to Paraguay local time, and counts a zone once even if both satellites see it. Users can explore the activity calendar, an interactive map and a department view. A citizen portal lets people report smoke or flames, and a private firefighter panel helps verify those reports.
It matters because it gives communities and emergency teams one clear, understandable picture of fire activity, helping prioritize where to verify first. A satellite detection is an indication, not a confirmation, and FIREGUARD does not replace firefighters.
details:
What it does and how it works. FIREGUARD is a web app that turns NASA FIRMS fire detections from two sensors, MODIS and VIIRS, into one daily fire-activity calendar for Paraguay. The sensors can’t be compared directly: they have different pixel sizes (1 km and 375 m), different confidence scales, and times in UTC. Our server unifies confidence into low, nominal and high, converts timestamps to Paraguay local time (UTC−3), and counts ~2 km “activity cells,” so a fire seen by both sensors or by several passes counts once. Each day is compared with the same days (±3) in earlier years to flag unusual activity. Users pick a day and see its detection cells on a Leaflet map. A citizen portal lets people report smoke or flames and follow the report with a code. A private firefighter panel lets responders verify reports, see satellite alerts near them, and review a history.

Benefits. One clear measure instead of two incompatible counts; a way to prioritize where to verify first; a transparent, documented method built only on public NASA data.

Intended impact. To help citizens, journalists, researchers and fire services in Paraguay see when fire activity is unusual and coordinate on-the-ground verification. FIREGUARD does not replace firefighters or emergency services.

Tools. JavaScript (Node.js server), HTML and CSS, Leaflet, OpenStreetMap, NASA GIBS imagery, and the NASA FIRMS API (MODIS_NRT, VIIRS_SNPP_NRT, MODIS_SP, VIIRS_SNPP_SP). Hosted on Render with PostgreSQL. 25 automated tests with Node’s built-in test runner. Developed with AI assistance (Claude, by Anthropic) for code and text; detections come only from NASA FIRMS.

Creativity. The activity-cell approach makes sensors of different resolution comparable. We also use log-scale anomalies against a multi-year baseline, and combine satellite hints with citizen reports.

Factors we considered. Honesty: real data only, never simulated, and a satellite detection is an indication, not a confirmation. Security: the NASA key stays on the server. Privacy: contact details are visible only to firefighters, and the public map hides free text and rounds locations. Abuse: rate limits and anti-spam. Accessibility: status is never shown by color alone. Limits: clouds and satellite pass times can hide fires, and recent and historical products can differ slightly. FIREGUARD is independent and is not created or endorsed by NASA.
